chapter: Ch 4: Presentation and Disclosures Based Accounting Standards
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction & Key Definitions under AS 20
explain: AS 20 sets principles for calculating and presenting Earnings Per Share (EPS) in the Statement of Profit and Loss.
It improves comparison of performance across different companies (inter-firm) and over different periods for the same company (intra-firm).
The standard is mandatory for all companies; however, Small and Medium-sized Companies (SMCs) are exempt from mandatory disclosure of Diluted EPS.
An equity share is any share other than a preference share.
A preference share carries preferential rights to receive dividend and repayment of capital.
A potential equity share is a financial instrument or contract entitling its holder to equity shares (e.g., convertible debentures, stock options).
Partly paid-up shares not entitled to dividends are treated as potential equity shares for Diluted EPS.

flow.title: Classification of Financial Assets and Potential Equity Shares
steps: Contract giving rights to equity or cash
Identify if cash asset or equity instrument
Check entitling rights to future equity
Classify as Potential Equity Share for EPS

topics.example: Company A issues debentures that can be converted into equity shares after 2 years. These convertible debentures are potential equity shares.
remember: AS 20 applies to all companies, but SMCs are exempt from mandatory Diluted EPS disclosure.
Partly paid shares without dividend rights are treated as potential equity shares.
mistakes: Treating preference shares as equity shares when calculating basic EPS.
Assuming SMCs cannot disclose Diluted EPS; they are allowed and encouraged to do so voluntarily.

quiz.q: Which of the following is treated as a potential equity share under AS 20?
o: Non-convertible preference shares
Options under Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs)
Fully paid equity shares
Bank loans with fixed interest
quiz.why: Stock options entitle holders to acquire equity shares, making them potential equity shares under AS 20.

quiz.q: Is disclosure of Diluted EPS mandatory for Small and Medium Companies (SMCs) under AS 20?
o: Yes, mandatory for all companies without exception
No, it is not mandatory for SMCs, though encouraged
Yes, but only if extraordinary items are present
No, SMCs are strictly prohibited from disclosing EPS
quiz.why: Disclosure of diluted EPS is not mandatory for SMCs under AS 20, though they are encouraged to make these disclosures.

topics.title: Basic EPS - Numerator (Earnings)
explain: Basic EPS formula: Net Profit or Loss Attributable to Equity Shareholders divided by Weighted Average Number of Equity Shares.
Net profit includes all tax expenses, exceptional items, and extraordinary items recognized in the period.
Preference dividends and attributable tax are deducted from net profit to arrive at net profit attributable to equity shareholders.
For non-cumulative preference shares, deduct dividend only if provided for in the books for the current period.
For cumulative preference shares, deduct the full required dividend for the current period, whether provided/declared or not.
Do not deduct cumulative preference dividends paid during the current period for previous financial years.
If a company has multiple classes of equity shares, net profit is apportioned according to their dividend rights.

flow.title: Numerator Adjustment Steps for Basic EPS
steps: Start with Net Profit after tax
Deduct non-cumulative preference dividend if provided
Deduct full cumulative preference dividend for current year
Arrive at Profit attributable to Equity Shareholders

topics.example: Company B earns Rs. 10,00,000 net profit. It has 10% cumulative preference shares of Rs. 2,00,000. Dividend of Rs. 20,000 is deducted even if not declared, leaving Rs. 9,80,000 for equity shareholders.
remember: Cumulative preference dividend is ALWAYS deducted for the current period only.
Past arrears of cumulative preference dividend paid now are ignored.
mistakes: Deducting non-cumulative preference dividend even when it was not provided for in the accounts.
Deducting cumulative preference dividend paid for past years in the current year's numerator.

quiz.q: How is cumulative preference dividend treated when calculating the numerator for Basic EPS if dividends are not declared?
o: Ignored completely until declared
Fully deducted for the current period
Added back to net profit
Deducted only up to 50%
quiz.why: Full required cumulative preference dividend for the current period is deducted whether declared or not.

quiz.q: When a company has more than one class of equity shares with different dividend rights:
o: Calculate a single combined EPS for all classes
Apportion net profit according to dividend rights and calculate separate EPS
Ignore preference dividend deduction
Use face value ratio without considering dividend rights
quiz.why: Net profit is apportioned over different classes of shares in accordance with their dividend rights, resulting in EPS for each class.

topics.title: Basic EPS - Denominator (Weighted Average Shares & Specific Issues)
explain: The denominator is the weighted average number of equity shares outstanding during the accounting period.
Time-weighting factor equals the number of days shares are outstanding divided by total days in the period.
Shares issued for cash are included from the date cash is receivable.
In amalgamation (purchase nature), shares are included from the acquisition date.
In amalgamation (merger nature), shares are included from the beginning of the reporting period.
Partly paid equity shares entitled to proportional dividends are treated as a fraction of an equity share.
Bonus issues and share splits increase shares without extra resources; they are adjusted retrospectively from the beginning of the earliest period reported.
A rights issue at less than fair value includes a bonus element. Multiply prior period shares by adjustment factor = (Fair value prior to rights) / (Theoretical ex-rights fair value).

flow.title: Determining Denominator for Basic EPS
steps: Start with opening equity shares
Add time-weighted new shares issued for cash
Apply retrospective adjustment for bonus/split
Compute total Weighted Average Equity Shares

topics.example: Company C had 1,800 shares on Jan 1, issued 600 shares for cash on May 31, and bought back 300 shares on Nov 1. Weighted average shares = (1,800 x 5/12) + (2,400 x 5/12) + (2,100 x 2/12) = 2,100 shares.
remember: Bonus issues and share splits require restatement of prior period EPS.
Rights issue adjustment factor = Fair value before rights / Theoretical ex-rights value.
mistakes: Time-weighting bonus shares from the date of issue instead of treating them as issued from the beginning of the period.
Including merger amalgamation shares only from the acquisition date instead of the beginning of the reporting period.

quiz.q: In an amalgamation in the nature of merger, equity shares issued as consideration are included in weighted average shares from:
o: The date of acquisition
The beginning of the reporting period
The date of agreement approval
The end of the financial year
quiz.why: In merger nature amalgamation, financial statements are prepared as if combined entity existed from the beginning, so shares are included from the beginning of the period.

quiz.q: What is the formula for the adjustment factor in a rights issue with a bonus element?
o: Theoretical ex-rights value / Exercise price
Fair value prior to exercise of rights / Theoretical ex-rights fair value
Exercise price / Fair value prior to rights
Number of new shares / Total old shares
quiz.why: The adjustment factor for restating prior period shares in a rights issue is Fair Value Prior to Exercise / Theoretical Ex-Rights Fair Value.

topics.title: Diluted EPS - Concept & Computation
explain: Diluted EPS shows the EPS if all dilutive potential equity shares were converted into equity shares.
Adjust Numerator: Add back interest on convertible debentures (net of tax) and preference dividends saved due to potential conversion.
Adjust Denominator: Add weighted average additional equity shares resulting from conversion of potential shares.
Potential shares are assumed to be converted at the beginning of the period or date of issue, whichever is later.
Share application money pending allotment (not statutorily kept separately and used in business) is treated as dilutive potential equity shares.
Stock options/ESOPs are dilutive if exercise price < average fair value.
Options are split into: shares issued at fair value (no dilution effect) and shares issued for no consideration (added to denominator).

flow.title: Diluted EPS Calculation Steps
steps: Take Net Profit for Basic EPS
Add after-tax interest/dividends saved on conversion
Take Weighted Shares for Basic EPS
Add incremental shares from conversion/options
Divide adjusted profit by adjusted shares

topics.example: Company D has net profit of Rs. 1,00,00,000 and 50,00,000 shares. It has 1,00,000 convertible debentures saving Rs. 8,40,000 after tax interest and converting to 10,00,000 shares. Diluted EPS = 1,08,40,000 / 60,00,000 = Rs. 1.81.
remember: Interest saved on convertible debt must be added back NET OF TAX.
Free shares under stock options = Total Options - (Total Options x Exercise Price / Fair Value).
mistakes: Adding back gross interest expense without deducting attributable tax expense.
Adding the entire option shares to denominator instead of only the bonus/free portion.

quiz.q: When calculating the numerator for Diluted EPS, interest expense on convertible debentures is:
o: Deducted gross from net profit
Added back to net profit net of tax
Ignored completely
Added back gross without tax adjustment
quiz.why: Interest saved on conversion is added back to net profit after adjusting for attributable tax expense.

quiz.q: Under AS 20, share options are dilutive when their exercise price is:
o: Greater than the average fair value of shares
Less than the average fair value of shares
Equal to the face value of shares
Zero
quiz.why: Options are dilutive when shares are issued for less than fair value, meaning exercise price < fair value.

topics.title: Dilutive vs Anti-Dilutive Potential Equity Shares
explain: Potential equity shares are dilutive if conversion decreases EPS (or increases loss per share) from continuing ordinary operations.
Anti-dilutive potential shares increase EPS (or decrease loss per share) from continuing ordinary operations and are IGNORED in Diluted EPS.
The 'control factor' for testing dilution is net profit or loss from continuing ordinary activities.
If a company has a profit from continuing operations, any potential share that reduces this profit per share is dilutive.
When there are multiple potential equity shares, test each series separately from most dilutive to least dilutive.
To sequence potential shares, calculate earnings per incremental potential equity share; the lowest incremental EPS is most dilutive.

flow.title: Testing for Dilutive Potential Shares
steps: Calculate EPS from continuing ordinary operations
Calculate incremental EPS for each potential share
Rank from lowest to highest incremental EPS
Include in Diluted EPS if it reduces EPS

topics.example: Company E has income from continuing operations of Rs. 2,40,000 and loss from discontinuing operations of Rs. 3,60,000 (net loss Rs. 1,20,000). The test for dilution uses Rs. 2,40,000, not the net loss.
remember: Control factor for dilution test = Profit/Loss from Continuing Ordinary Operations.
Anti-dilutive shares are excluded from Diluted EPS.
mistakes: Using final net profit/loss including discontinuing operations as the benchmark for dilution test.
Combining multiple potential equity shares together instead of testing them individually in sequence.

quiz.q: What is the benchmark control factor to determine whether potential equity shares are dilutive?
o: Net profit after extraordinary items
Profit or loss from continuing ordinary activities
Gross profit from sales
Total comprehensive income
quiz.why: AS 20 explicitly specifies that profit or loss from continuing ordinary activities is the control factor for dilution testing.

quiz.q: If conversion of a convertible bond increases EPS from continuing ordinary activities, the bond is:
o: Dilutive and included in Diluted EPS
Anti-dilutive and ignored in Diluted EPS
Treated as a bonus issue
Restated retrospectively
quiz.why: Conversion that increases EPS from continuing operations is anti-dilutive and must be ignored.

topics.title: Restatement, Presentation, and Disclosures
explain: Restatement: If bonus issue, share split, or reverse split occurs, EPS calculations for all presented periods must be adjusted.
If these changes happen after balance sheet date but before approval of financial statements by the Board, EPS figures in the financial statements must be restated.
Presentation: Basic and Diluted EPS must be presented on the face of the Statement of Profit and Loss with equal prominence for each class of equity shares.
EPS must be presented even if the figures are negative (i.e., loss per share).
Disclosure 1: Basic and Diluted EPS computed excluding extraordinary items (net of tax).
Disclosure 2: Numerator reconciliation to net profit/loss for the period.
Disclosure 3: Denominator reconciliation between basic and diluted EPS denominators.
Disclosure 4: Nominal value of shares along with EPS figures.

flow.title: Post-Balance Sheet Bonus Issue Workflow
steps: Bonus issue approved after balance sheet date
Occurs before Board approval of financial statements
Restate current and comparative Basic & Diluted EPS
Disclose fact of restatement on face of P&L

topics.example: Company F approves a 1:1 bonus issue on April 15 before financial statements for March 31 are signed. EPS for both current year and comparative previous year are restated based on doubled share count.
remember: Bonus/split after balance sheet date before Board approval requires EPS restatement.
Always disclose nominal value of shares alongside EPS.
mistakes: Failing to restate prior year comparative EPS when a bonus issue occurs.
Omitting EPS from face of P&L when the company incurs a net loss.

quiz.q: If a 1-for-1 bonus issue takes place after the balance sheet date but before the Board approves financial statements:
o: EPS of the current year only is adjusted
EPS of both current year and prior comparative period presented must be restated
No adjustment is made until next financial year
Only Diluted EPS is adjusted
quiz.why: AS 20 requires restatement of per share calculations for all periods presented if bonus issue occurs before financial statement approval.

quiz.q: Which of the following disclosures is NOT mandatory under AS 20?
o: Nominal value of shares
Reconciliation of numerators to net profit
Future projected EPS for next 3 years
Weighted average number of shares used as denominator
quiz.why: AS 20 requires historical numerators, denominators, reconciliations, and nominal values, not future projections.
